bodies.name: Ross 128 b
bodies.nativeSurface: RV detection; no resolved native scientific surface map located. Archive radius is a mass-radius estimate, not a measured radius.
measured: HARPS RV discovery gives a projected minimum mass of 1.35 Earth masses; current archive composite adopts 1.4 Earth masses and period 9.8658 days.
Host adopted in discovery: 3192±60 K, radius 0.1967±0.0077 solar radii.
modelled: Adopted archive semimajor axis 0.0496 AU; host 3192 K, 0.1967 solar radii.
Discovery equilibrium estimates span 213–269 K for different assumed albedos; archive 301 K uses another model. These are not measured ground temperatures.
unknown: Physical radius, inclination, true mass, spin, atmosphere, pressure, composition, surface accessibility, geography and visible colour.
Habitable-zone or temperature estimates do not establish habitability, oceans or life.
assumed: Hypothetical dry silicate/iron rocky body with a thin 0.2-bar nitrogen/carbon-dioxide atmosphere; gas mixture and pressure are invented, not measured.
Slate-grey fractured uplands, muted buff dust, independent volcanic plains and sparse shallow craters; all geography imagined.
Thin blue-grey haze and a warm cream/peach white star; scattering, exposure and material colour are artistic.
Invented north-up longitude frame and imperfect texture seam; no measured pole or physical terrain registration.
Nominal 60° horizontal camera field; semimajor-axis representative illumination is not a dated ephemeris.
Raster validation: bright-core widths 150/95/67 original pixels versus geometric target 53.42 pixels in a 1672-pixel image. Glare, star size and colour remain approximate; refinement open.

references.title: Bonfils et al., A temperate exo-Earth around a quiet M dwarf at 3.4 parsecs

surfaceMap.projection: 2:1 equirectangular north-up hypothesis; no measured terrain frame.

rasterValidation.method: Bright-core bounding box in central star-only ROI (x40–60%, y8–25%); R>180/210/240, G>150, B>80. Glare and photosphere cannot be fully separated.
rasterValidation.limits: Nominal 60° camera FOV is artistic; angular/raster scale and colour are not photometrically calibrated.

bodies.name: Gl 725 A b
bodies.nativeSurface: RV detection; no resolved native scientific surface map located. Archive radius is a mass-radius estimate, not a measured radius.
measured: Independent optical SOPHIE and near-infrared SPIRou RV signal: period 11.2201±0.0051 days, minimum mass 2.78±0.35 Earth masses, amplitude 1.67±0.20 m/s.
No transit found in 27 TESS sectors. Discovery manuscript calls this a candidate; NASA confirmed-planet composite includes it with discovery year 2025.
modelled: Adopted archive semimajor axis 0.068 AU; host 3433 K, 0.351 solar radii.
Archive equilibrium 376.1 K is a model, not measured surface temperature. Published radius predictions 1.2–2.0 Earth radii are mass-radius estimates, not transit measurements.
unknown: Physical radius, inclination, true mass, spin, atmosphere, pressure, composition, surface accessibility, geography and visible colour.
Habitable-zone or temperature estimates do not establish habitability, oceans or life.
assumed: Hypothetical dry airless silicate/iron surface; actual atmospheric presence and volatile inventory are unknown.
Ash-grey volcanic plates, charcoal braided fractures, shallow rounded basins and taupe regolith are wholly imagined; no active lava is inferred.
Black sky and warm cream star; binary companion B is outside the chosen artistic field. Binary orientation and scene epoch are not registered.
Invented north-up longitude frame and imperfect texture seam; no measured pole or physical terrain registration.
Nominal 60° horizontal camera field; semimajor-axis representative illumination is not a dated ephemeris.
Raster validation: bright-core widths 92/92/90 original pixels versus geometric target 69.54 pixels in a 1672-pixel image. Glare, star size and colour remain approximate; refinement open.

references.title: Cortés-Zuleta et al., Gl 725A b: a potential super-Earth detected with SOPHIE and SPIRou
references.observationDate: SOPHIE March 2021–December 2023; SPIRou February 2019–April 2022; detailed epochs in Appendix A; 27 TESS sectors examined.

surfaceMap.projection: 2:1 equirectangular north-up hypothesis; no measured terrain frame.

rasterValidation.method: Bright-core bounding box in central star-only ROI (x40–60%, y8–25%); R>180/210/240, G>150, B>80. Glare and photosphere cannot be fully separated.
rasterValidation.limits: Nominal 60° camera FOV is artistic; angular/raster scale and colour are not photometrically calibrated.
